etymologies.etymologyHTML: From out- +‎ set, replacing earlier outsetting.

definitions.definition: Onset; the beginning or initial stage of something. [from 1759]

quote.citation: 1881–1882, Robert Louis Stevenson, Treasure Island, London; Paris: Cassell & Company, published 14 November 1883, →OCLC:
quote.text: At the first outset, heavy, miry ground and a matted, marish vegetation greatly delayed our progress;  […]

quote.citation: 1954 January, “Notes and News: An Abandoned Railway from the Air”, in Railway Magazine, page 64:
quote.text: It was opened on July 1, 1903, and worked by the former Highland Railway from the outset.

quote.citation: 2011 October 15, Michael Da Silva, “Wigan 1 - 3 Bolton”, in BBC Sport‎[1]:
quote.text: Six successive defeats had left them rooted to the bottom of the Premier League table but, clearly under instructions to attack from the outset, Bolton started far the brighter.

etymologies.etymologyHTML: From out- +‎ set.

definitions.definition: (Internet, CSS, transitive) To cause (a design element) to extend around the outside of something else, the opposite of being inset.
